memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creating that he had done. — Gen 2:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what God does with the seventh day: He blesses it and makes it holy. This is the first time in the Bible that something is called "holy," and it is striking that God sets apart not a place or a person, but a day. To make something holy means to set it apart for a special purpose. God took this one day and marked it as different from the rest.

Why does this matter for us? It shows that God cares about more than just what we produce. He wove into the very rhythm of the world a time to stop, to remember Him, and to delight in what He has done. Long before the law was given to Israel, God was teaching that our lives are meant to have space for worship and rest, not endless activity.

We should hold this gently. As believers, we are not bound by rigid rules about which day or how (Col 2:16–17). But the principle remains beautiful and good. Every rhythm of rest we keep points forward to Jesus, who is our true Sabbath rest. In Him, we stop labouring to earn God's favour, because He has already secured it for us. So set aside time to be still before God. Let a portion of your week belong especially to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What would it look like to intentionally set apart time for God each week?
- Do you tend to view rest as wasted time, or as a gift from God?
- How does resting in Christ's finished work free you from striving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for blessing rest and making it holy. Help me to set apart time for You, not out of duty, but out of love, and to find my deepest rest in Jesus. Amen.
